newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-MICKELSON WINS SPRINT INTERNATIONAL, RYDER CUP SPOT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MICKELSON WINS SPRINT INTERNATIONAL, RYDER CUP SPOT.

text.p: Phil Mickelson claimed his second Sprint International title Sunday and nailed down a place on the U.S. Ryder Cup team in the process.

Mickelson, who led going into the final round, was never seriously challenged Sunday as he cruised to a seven-point victory over Australian Stuart Appleby in delightful playing conditions at Castle Pines.
He compiled five birdies and one bogey for a four-under-par 68 worth nine points under the Modified Stableford format used for the event.
The scoring system awards five points for eagle, two for birdie, zero for par, and subtracts one point for bogey and three for double bogey or worse.
Mickelson finished with 48 points to become the first two-time winner in the event's 12-year history and beat his own tournament record of 45 points, set in 1993.
He recorded two eagles, 21 birdies and four bogeys for an unofficial 21-under 267 total.

"I played four good rounds and that's something I haven't done too much this year. It gives me a bit of momentum going into the PGA Championship," said Mickelson of the year's final major championship in two weeks.
His 11th career PGA Tour victory and second of the year was worth $306,000 and 150 Ryder Cup points, which vaulted Mickelson from ninth to fifth place in the U.S. standings.
The top 10 players after the PGA Championship automatically make the American team that will challenge Cup holder Europe at Valderrama, Spain, next month.
Mickelson was delighted to clinch a Ryder Cup berth, but made it clear he was more concerned about the majors.
"The Ryder Cup is nice. I'm excited to be on the team but the four major championships mean a lot more to me, to be honest," he said.
"The disappointing thing after five years out here is I haven't won a major. Guys I grew up with and competed against are winning majors.
"This hasn't been the most spectacular of years, after last year winning four times. I hope to use this event as a stepping stone for the rest of the year."

Mickelson made an ideal start to the final round when he sank a 25-foot slider for birdie at the opening hole. He quickly added three more birdies, before recording his lone bogey of the day at the par-four ninth.

Skip Kendall birdied the 10th, 11th and 13th holes to reduce the margin to five points -- which could be erased with one eagle. But when Mickelson birdied the par-five 14th it was just about all over.

Kendall self-destructed over the final holes to finish third on 38 points, leaving the fast-finishing Appleby, who eagled the 14th and birdied the final two holes, to vault into second place on 41 points.
"I'm happy with second. It wasn't like I had a big chance today," said Appleby, who also finished second to Mickelson at the Bay Hill Invitational in March.
